items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Sid say, 'Come on, brother, let's go back to Louis Armstrong. Let's go with Louis.' ... Anyway, I went with Big Sid.

ctx.x: He didn't fine him, either. So now, we're at Frank Daly, you know, Pee Wee's helping Benny to change, helping him to dress, rather. And Sid and I were over in another corner, watching a checker game, with our backs turned.
So Benny asked Sid, he says, "Sid," he says, "What happened with that boy, Gillespie in Cab Calloway? Sid says, mum-mum-mum-mum, and when he said that, he tore out of the dressing room.

items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Sid Catlett and John Simmons, they fired when they get to Chicago... Big Sid snatched me out of my shoes. He said, 'Man, you hit that man in his mouth, you'll never play another note of music in your life.'

ctx.x: Well, Smiley was almost as tall as Sid, but he didn't have the weight that Sid had. Sid hit him once, he went down. And Sid -- that's the first time I've ever seen him angry. People said a whole lot of things to him, but he just couldn't stand Bob because he knew that Bob was a snitch, you know.

So Louis says, 'Let 'em fight.' Velva - Middleton went into hysterics, 'They're fighting, they're fighting, they're fighting.' He started to say the magic word, Louis did. 'Let 'em fight, let 'em fight.' Bus driver almost run the bus off the road. 'Let 'em fight. Sid Catlett and John Simmons, they fired when they get to Chicago.' I said, 'John Simmons? How did I come into this?' Dumb, you know? 'I still say John Simmons. You and Big Sid Catlett, would-be pimps and press hogs, gamblers. You're fired when you get…
